decisive_items: A small extension of high signal from the lateral aspect of one lesion resembled a “mouse-tail.”
The lesions followed the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves without evidence of invasion.
response.rationale: The imaging findings (T1 isointense, T2 hyperintense with rim, mouse-tail sign) and linear distribution along plantar digital nerves strongly favor plexiform schwannoma. Neurofibroma is less likely given no NF history and similar but less specific features. Glomus tumor is unsupported by the multiple nerve-associated nodules and imaging pattern.

rejected.why: Imaging shows multiple nerve-associated nodules with mouse-tail sign, not typical for glomus tumor; cold sensitivity is nonspecific.
No family history of neurofibromatosis and imaging features (homogeneous T2 hyperintensity with rim, mouse-tail) are more characteristic of plexiform schwannoma than neurofibroma.
